title: A study to identify new blood markers that could help assess immune system activity in people with type 2 diabetes and foot ulcers
official: Novel blood markers for the assessment of NETosis in type 2 diabetes patients with foot ulcers
summary:
Background and study aims
Neutrophils in blood defend the body against bacteria and infection. Neutrophils do this by engulfing the bacteria, that is, releasing their DNA strands out of the cell as a net to trap the bacteria (NETosis). The enzymes positioned on the DNA strands can then kill the bacteria in blood without harming the other cells in the body. The changes in the level of
the enzymes and proteins associated with the net and trap in the blood can be used as a marker of healing or deterioration of foot ulcers in patients with diabetes. So far there are no specific diagnostic kits to measure NETs formation during infection. The new assay acquired from Volition company will allow this measurement. We would like to measure the formation of the NETS in the blood and the activity of NETosis in the blood in vitro in patients suffering from diabetic foot ulcers to establish the significance of this activity in diabetes and infection in blood. 

Who can participate?
We will have 3 groups of participants with type 2 diabetes with different levels of diabetes control and foot ulcers and a group of healthy people as control group, to investigate the effect of type 2 diabetes on NETS formation.

What does the study involve?
The participants will be asked to attend one session lasting approximately one hour, during which a physical examination will be conducted and a blood sample will be collected

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Possible benefits:
We hope to demonstrate that the measurement of NETs may help doctors manage patients with infection, particularly foot ulcers and predict how they respond to treatment. Perhaps by measuring circulatory NETs formation would be possible to show in future whether a patient with foot ulcer is responding to a specific medication or not and predict the outcome. We might be able to look into how patients with diabetes respond to infection.

Risks associated with the procedure:
1. The risks of having a butterfly needle in a vein are associated with minor discomfort, possible bruising and, in principle, a local infection
2. Blood testing is part of normal diabetes care. However, you may experience slight discomfort, and some people do experience bruising after a blood sample has been taken. The total amount of blood to be taken will be about 28.5 mL, about 2 tablespoons. If you feel ill or experience any unusual discomfort, it is important that you inform the study team as soon as possible. If the study doctor feels that there is medical or safety concerns, your participation may be stopped 
3. You will be able to telephone the study team if you experience any unwanted side effects and require medical advice

Where is the study run from?
CEDAR , Royal Surrey Hospital (UK).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
December 2026 to December 2027. 

Who is funding the study?
Volition Diagnostics Ltd. (UK).

Who is the main contact?
Dr Fariba Shojaee-Moradie, f.shojaee-moradie@nhs.net

interventions.name:
This will be a cross-sectional study investigating the formation of NETs in the blood of patients with well- and poorly controlled type 2 diabetes presenting with or without diabetic foot ulcer, in comparison to healthy adults (as a marker of low NETs levels in blood).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
There will be 4 groups of people. 
For eligible participants in all 4 groups all the following criteria must be answered 'yes'
1. Participants aged 18-85 years inclusive
2. BMI of less than 45 kg/m²
3. Able to comply with the study and give informed consent
4. Patients who are or who have previously been involved in research are eligible provided a participant has not received an investigational drug within one month of entry into the study

In addition to the above criteria, each group has specific requirements as follows and must be answered 'yes':
Group 1. Participants with type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months) within 2 months of presentation of a foot ulcer:
1.1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes greater than 12 months
1.2. New presentation of an ulcer with a history of duration not exceeding two months

Group 2. Participants with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months) without foot ulcer:
2.1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes greater than 12 months
2.2. HbA1C >=68 mmol/mol inc

Group 3. Participants with well-controlled type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months)  without foot ulcer:
3.1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes greater than 12 months
3.2. HbA1c <58 mmol/mol inc

Group 4. Healthy participants:
4.1. HbA1c <42 mmol/mol
4.2. Recruited  into two subgroups of BMI <30 kg/m² and >=30 BMI<45 kg/m² with n=10 in each group
Exclusion criteria:
There will be 4 groups of people. 
For eligible participants in all 4 groups all the following criteria must be answered ‘No’
1.	Participants over 85 or under 18 years
2.	Having diagnosis of type 1 diabetes
3.	Having diagnosis of type 3C diabetes
4.	Having diagnosis of pre-diabetes
5.	Participants who cannot adequately understand verbal and / or written explanations given in English
6.	Confirmed excessive and compulsive drinking of alcohol i.e. alcohol abuse as determined from GP medical notes by Fast Alcohol Screening Test (FAST) or history of previous alcohol abuse
7.	Any acute and currently treated infection of HIV, Hepatitis B, C or TB
8.	Any acute infection (e.g., bacterial or viral), excluding diabetic foot ulcers in Group 1
9.	Steroid therapy
10.	No Microvascular disease excluding Group 1
11.	Autoimmune inflammatory diseases (RA, colitis, pancreatitis) requiring active treatment
12.	Mental incapacity
13.	Pregnancy or those females of child-bearing potential not taking adequate contraception precautions, or breast-feeding women (adequate protection is defined as barrier protection, oral contraceptive pill or intrauterine device)
14.	Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS), acute stroke or TIA within 2 months prior to enrolment
15.	Are not primarily responsible for their own care
16.	Acute malignancy under active treatment

In addition to the above criteria each group has specific requirements as follows and must also be answered ‘No’:
Group 1. Participants with type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months) within 2 months of presentation of a foot ulcer:
No other exclusion criteria

Group 2.participant with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months) without foot ulcer:
2.1.	Having foot ulcer
2.2.	HbA1c  <68 mmol/mol

Group 3. participant with well-controlled type 2 diabetes (with diagnosis over 12 months) without foot ulcer:
3.1.	Having foot ulcer
3.2.	HbA1c >58 mmol/mol

Group 4. Healthy participants:
4.1.	Having diabetes diagnosis (HbA1c >=42 mmol/mol)
4.2.	Having a foot ulcer
